top.line: Each row of an agent's policy gets a vendor's share
top.para: Part of an agent's risk is the vendor's: the model's answer, the guardrail that let something through. Today's terms cap vendors at a year's fees; Europe makes software a product from 9 December 2026. The proposal: a vendor's share per row, £1,816 of £6,720 in the example.

in-short.line: Eight lines from two parties to the vault
in-short.para: Part of the risk is the vendor's; the cloud already splits it; two contracts cap at a year's fees; Microsoft's guardrail condition is the shape; Europe moves the line; each row gets a vendor's layer; £1,816 of £6,720; the formula is a vault.

two-parties.line: Every row has a vendor and a customer in it
two-parties.para: The customer granted write access, so corrupted records are its row; the vendor's model gave the wrong answer, and its filter let the leak through. The vendor should carry a share of the rows its product decides, up to an amount it names.

shared.line: Of the agent is the vendor's; in the agent, the customer's
shared.para: AWS splits security of the cloud from security in the cloud. For an agent the vendor answers for the model, guardrails, updates and security, and the customer for the grant, data, controls and runtime; the line runs through each row and moves with the controls.

terms.line: Two contracts cap at a year's fees and leave outputs
terms.para: Anthropic's terms limit liability to 12 months' fees, indemnify IP and leave outputs to the customer; Salesforce caps at twelve months and its AI policy makes safe use the customer's. No Agentforce cover was found; a year's fees is small beside £80,000 of rows.

started.line: Cover on a condition, and guarantees on performance
started.para: Microsoft pays copyright claims if the customer used its guardrails: the vendor's layer for one row. Intercom offers up to $1M back for Fin; Sierra and Zendesk price by outcome; ElevenLabs has AIUC-1-backed cover; Munich Re sells vendors performance warranties.

europe.line: From 9 December 2026, software is a product in the EU
europe.para: The product liability directive names AI system providers as manufacturers, keeps update and cybersecurity defects within their control theirs, and bars contractual caps against injured persons, who must be natural persons. The AI Act splits duties between provider and deployer.

layer.line: A share per row, paid when the vendor's conditions held
layer.para: Corrupted records 0%, the customer's grant; leaked data 20%, the vendor's filter; a wrong answer 50%, the vendor's product. The vendor carries £1,816 of £6,720 with its guardrails on, nothing with them off; the shell row is excluded for both.

vault.line: The formula, the inputs and a calculator in a vault
vault.para: The vault holds the seven steps, every input, a script that reproduces every number in the series, and a calculator to switch controls, change limits and the vendor's share, and test a claim. A control nothing enforces moves nothing.

next.line: Questions for vendors, insurers and policy writers
next.para: Which rows vendors would carry and on what conditions; whether insurers would price the customer's and the vendor's layers as separate books; and a field for the vendor's share and its conditions beside each row of a behaviour policy.

limits.line: Illustrative shares, two contracts, not legal advice
limits.para: The shares are not negotiated; two published contracts are not the market; the directive's application from December 2026 is open; absences mean none was found; the copyright commitments are cited for their shape only.

sources.line: Two memos, research agents and the vault
sources.para: From the first two memos of the series; sources fetched on 28 October 2026, EU texts via the Publications Office, OpenAI described from press coverage; the vault's sources are kept in the repository notes.
